proof:
As in the arbitrary concave-buffer quantile result 0b2fbdaf8d3134a0, each nonvertical $Q$-superlevel condition is $H(w)-\varepsilon G(u)f(w)\le c_Q(H)$, with $c_Q(H)$ the right $Q$-quantile of $H(z,X)=a\cdot z+u\cdot X$. By 5aeb5916857f97a9 and continuity of the energy on the hull, $f=M^{-1/N}(E^{1/d})^{d/N}L^{1/N}$ is continuous and concave. The pure-base superlevel is convex as well, so $w_0$ is deepest and $I$ is a closed minor. All deepest marks are own-interior because the zero-boundary profile gives zero depth there. At a proper mark, 20210aa9d661295a gives an attaining nonvertical cap with proper own trace, while 3dd858960f824a5d shows that every own buffered trace at an atomic deepest mark is full.

Take any minimizing nonvertical cap at $w_0$, normalized by $G(u)=1$. The proper own trace implies strict decrease of the cap tail near its threshold $c=H(w_0)-\varepsilon f(w_0)$, hence $c=c_Q(H)$. At each input $H(w_j)-\varepsilon f(w_j)\le c$. Averaging yields $f(w_0)\le\sum_j\lambda_j f(w_j)$. Concavity forces equality and every input threshold to equal $c$. Set $F_j=E_{K_{p_j}}(y_j)^{1/d}$, with the analogous $F_0$. The affinity identity $L_0=\sum_j\lambda_j L_j$ and the energy-root lower bound give
$$
F_0^{d/N}L_0^{1/N}\ge
\Big(\sum_j\lambda_j F_j\Big)^{d/N} L_0^{1/N}
\ge \sum_j\lambda_j F_j^{d/N}L_j^{1/N}.
$$
Equality implies $F_0=\sum_j\lambda_jF_j$ and constant $F_j/L_j$, by strict Jensen for the power $d/N$ with weights $\lambda_j L_j/L_0$. By 5aeb5916857f97a9 the actual target fiber equals the Minkowski combination and the centered inputs are positive homothets. The scaling law of d90ba05577427854 identifies the homothety scales with the $F_j$, so the fibers at the marks have the asserted form and their common proper trace excludes any atomic input. On a fixed own interior the energy root is strictly concave by 5aeb5916857f97a9. The geometric mean preserves this strictness because $L$ is positive affine and the mean is increasing in the energy root. Two distinct proper deepest marks on the same base would therefore contradict the equality just proved at their midpoint.

If an integer base in $P$ is in $\operatorname{conv}J$, it is deepest, and every closed pure-base cap through it contains at least one of the proper input bases. Its base depth is at least the minimum of their base depths, strictly larger than $Q$. If an integer base lies in $\operatorname{conv}A$, it is deepest and cannot be proper by the input heredity just proved. Thus both strata are closed minors. For $A\ne\varnothing$ and $Q<M$, efc6257ea1f83bc1 supplies a cover by exact mass-$Q$ caps with exclusive boundary witnesses in $A$ of distinct parities. No cap contains a point of $J$ by its larger base depth. If one witness shared parity with $p\in J$, their midpoint would be an integer point in $I$ strictly outside all covering caps. It would have to be in $J$, violating heredity. This proves the claimed count. If $Q=M$, all proper bases are absent and $P$ is a singleton, since on any larger base a pure-base cap through a given point can exclude another point of positive weight. The whole-base cap then supplies the count. The empty $A$ needs no cap.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty complete base in an affine lattice, with positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ ($d\ge1$) satisfying the anchored Minkowski inclusions $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_z$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, $dm=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. All affine functions are relative to $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^d$. Let $\varepsilon>0$, $N=d+1$, and $G(u)=(M^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_z}[u\cdot(X-g_z)]^2\,dX)^{1/2}$, where $g_z$ are the fiber centroids. Use marked energy $E_K(y)=\inf_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-d-1}\,dX$ over denominators strictly positive throughout $K$, extended by zero on $\partial K$. For a parameter $L$ put $f(z,y)=[L(z,y)E_{K_z}(y)/M]^{1/N}$ and use the infimum $b_L(p,y)$ of mixed masses of the caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon G(u)f(p,y),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (including the whole-base trace). Write $b_{\rm base}(p)$ for the latter minimum alone. Let $Q=\max_S b_L$, $I$ be the bases of maximizing marks, $J=\{p\in I:b_{\rm base}(p)>Q\}$, $A=I\setminus J$, and $k(T)$ count inherited lattice parities occupied by $T$, with $k(\varnothing)=0$. Assume $L$ is affine and strictly positive on $C$, with $M^{-1}\int_S L^{-r}\,dm=1$ for a fixed $r\ge d$.

Suppose $Q>0$ and $p_0=\sum_j\lambda_jp_j\in J$ is an anchored convex combination of deepest bases $p_j\in I$ with $\lambda_j>0$. For any corresponding deepest marks $w_j=(p_j,y_j)$ the affine combination $w_0=(p_0,y_0)=\sum_j\lambda_jw_j$ is deepest. All inputs lie in $J$. With $L_j=L(w_j)$ and $L_0=L(w_0)$, there is a convex body $D$ with $K_{p_j}=y_j+L_jD$, $K_{p_0}=y_0+L_0D$ and $f(w_j)/L_j=f(w_0)/L_0=c_*>0$. An active cap at $w_0$, with $G(u)=1$, is active at all these marks and its own traces are the same proper set $\{Y\in D:u\cdot Y\ge-\varepsilon c_*\}$ in those normalized fibers. Each $p\in J$ has a unique deepest mark. Both $J$ and $A$ are closed minors, and $A$ has a closed pure-base cover of at most $k(I)-k(J)$ caps of exact mass $Q$.
title: Marked homothety and parity compression for full-affine buffers
